title: A punctured set that is locally an m-plane of the (m+1)-space A₀ is a punctured m-plane (parent steps 2, 5–8)
statement: Globalization. Data: P, m ∈ ℕ; a linear subspace A₀ ⊆ ℝ^P; M ⊆ ℝ^P. Hypotheses: m ≥ 2; dim A₀ = m + 1; M ≠ ∅; 0 ∉ M; closure(M) ⊆ M ∪ {0}; and for every x ∈ M there are a linear subspace H ⊆ A₀ with dim H = m and an open set O ⊆ ℝ^P with x ∈ O and O ∩ M = O ∩ H. Conclusion: there is a linear subspace H₀ ⊆ ℝ^P with dim H₀ = m (Module.finrank ℝ H₀ = m) and M = H₀ ∖ {0}.
lean_statement: ∀ (P m : ℕ) (A₀ : Submodule ℝ (Euclid P)) (M : Set (Euclid P)), 2 ≤ m → Module.finrank ℝ A₀ = m + 1 → M.Nonempty → (0 : Euclid P) ∉ M → closure M ⊆ insert 0 M → (∀ x ∈ M, ∃ H : Submodule ℝ (Euclid P), Module.finrank ℝ H = m ∧ H ≤ A₀ ∧ ∃ O : Set (Euclid P), IsOpen O ∧ x ∈ O ∧ O ∩ M = O ∩ (H : Set (Euclid P))) → ∃ H₀ : Submodule ℝ (Euclid P), Module.finrank ℝ H₀ = m ∧ M = (H₀ : Set (Euclid P)) \ {0}
